newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh urgently needs to lure investment - report.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh urgently needs to lure investment - report.

text.p: Bangladesh, seeking to attain rapid industrial and economic development, needs to make drastic policy reforms to lure foreign investment, local and foreign experts said on Tuesday.
The experts attending an investment seminar in Dhaka said the inflow of foreign direct investment into Bangladesh was far below potential even though the country offered high returns.

"The government should initiate a continuing dialogue with the existing foreign direct investors in the country so as to ascertain why this is the case," said a report prepared at the three-day seminar which ended in Dhaka on Monday.
It was organised jointly by the Bangladesh Board of Investment (BOI) and the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP).

"The seminar noted with satisfaction that Bangladesh offered a high rate of return to foreign investment...and the measures adopted so far to attract FDI (foreign direct investment)," said the report, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
"(However), there was an urgent need to evolve political and social consensus on the role of FDI in accelerating the country's pace of economic development."
According to World Investment Report, the flow of foreign direct investment into the country was $14 million in 1993 and $11 million in 1994.
FDI proposals increased to more than $1.5 billion in 1995/96 (July-June), according to official figures.

The seminar called for an "integrated approach for attaining macro-economic stability and development of human resources, private sector, infrastructure, privatisation and administrative and legal reforms to create an efficient and transparent system.

"There is a need to further harmonise various policy measures," the report said. "Aggressive and sustained efforts should be mounted to persuade the investing countries to relocate their manufacturing activities to Bangladesh," it said.

The seminar also recommended "immediate steps" to privatise all support services in gas and oil exploration, telecommunication, ports and inland waterways and power sectors which were still owned by the government.

It suggested cuts in tariff and non-tariff barriers on import of capital goods for the expansion of manufacturing and service industries as well as oil and gas, power, telecommunication and port facilities.
"The return for investing in Bangladesh is very high...50 percent or more in the manufacturing sector," said Forrest E. Cookson, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh.

"Many foreign observers anticipate that FDI in Bangladesh would surge over the next 10 years, mainly in labour-intensive industrial and infrastructure sectors," said Koya Haruhara of ESCAP's Industry and Technology division.

Sharif M. Afzal Hossain, president of the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries, said: "It's true that foreign investment has not grown much in Bangladesh but the interest of investors is enough. They are particularly eager to invest in oil and gas and telecommunications."
